answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to post a per-epoch non-refundable stake that burns on failed attestation. Each new agent must lock collateral, and peers grade its work: a swarm of copycat accounts must each pay that entry fee, so a thousand-node attack costs a thousand times one honest bond. The fee is set well above the marginal reward, making fakery unprofitable. An honest agent recovers its stake only when peer votes hold as a steady anchor; a fraudulent plume of lookalikes instead forfeits every bond. Attacks become a costly fable, not a cheap rumor.
